newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Oct 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Oct 1.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Chart Thai party secretary-general Snoh Thienthong has agreed to lead a mass defection to the New Aspiration Party, which has made generous offers to potential defectors in its bid to sweep the Nov 17 election. (BANGKOK POST/THE NATION)

- The Democrat Party is making its leader Chuan Leekpai the main theme of its election campaign, asking voters to choose the party's candidates if they want Chuan to become prime minister. Several slogans for the campaign in Bangkok have been conceived using Chuan's name. (THE NATION)

- Four districts of the central province of Petchaburi have been flooded after two dams overflowed following heavy rain. Meanwhile, the Highways Department has said that 14 highways nationwide have been made impassable by floods following several days of downpours. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand has decided to cancel its plans to buy electricity from Laos after private investors in the scheme want to postpone sales of the electricity to another two years. (KRUNGTHEP THURAKIJ)
- Negotiations with Nithipat Capital Group, which wants to acquire 30 percent of the shares in Bangkok Bank of Commerce, will be concluded in a few weeks. (BANGKOK POST)

- TelecomAsia Corp Plc will soon negotiate with the Telephone Organisation of Thailand TOT) to install and operate the Personal Handy Phone System service for the TOT's 2.5 million lines nationwide. The TOT is studying the legal and technical aspects of the proposed three-party joint venture to provide PHS services for one million telephone users as early as 1997. (BUSINESS DAY)
